note: What every containment frame draws in its title tab. The rule is one line: a frame's badge is the vendor's own artwork for that boundary, and where the vendor ships none the frame takes the generic tab. A near-miss icon is worse than no icon -- it states something false, the way Azure's Availability Sets mark did when it stood in for an Availability Zone. Every blank below is a recorded decision with its reason, not an oversight.
source_of_truth: The themes under assets/themes/*.json carry boundaries.icons, which is what the renderers read. This file is the reviewed record of that map, and tests/unit/test_frame_badges.py fails when the two disagree, so a theme cannot gain or lose a badge without somebody deciding to.

aws.note: The deck files thirteen icons as group boxes. Every badge here is one of them: the group box for that boundary, never the service icon of the same name and never a mark from a third-party logo pack.

exceptions.organization: the deck ships no Organizations group box, but AWS's own reference diagrams draw the organization boundary with the Organizations service icon, in the same #e7157b as the account box; this is the one AWS badge that is a service icon rather than a group box, and it is allowed by name

blank.zone: Azure ships Availability Sets artwork and no Availability Zone artwork, and the two are different things: a set spreads across fault domains inside one datacenter, a zone is a separate datacenter. Drawing a zone with the set icon states something false

reasons.cloud: Azure ships no group box for the cloud itself; the frame is Azure, and wears Azure's own mark from the vendor's icon set, the way the AWS Cloud frame wears the AWS logo
